methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $500M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Wandelbots, a Series G robotics and manufacturing automation company, has raised $126M to date. The valuation landscape for frontier robotics comprises a sparse set of public and private comparables: one public peer and eight private companies including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, direct peer-median triangulation is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds for statistical reliability.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable lens. Using total capital raised ($126M) as a valuation proxy yields a $500M baseline, to which a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement is applied, implying a valuation of $625M. This method reflects the accumulated investor capital and expected equity dilution patterns at this stage.

Given the single-method triangulation, the analysis supports a valuation range of $531M to $719M, with a median point estimate of $625M. This range incorporates symmetric sensitivity around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable transaction data at equivalent stages within the narrow robotics automation segment, which limits calibration precision. Investor conviction should weight the reliability of stage-based multiples against Wandelbots' specific unit economics, capital efficiency, and product-market positioning within the robotics sector.
